precepts.text: And I will set my face against you, and ye shall be slain before your enemies: they that hate you shall reign over you; and ye shall flee when none pursueth you. That is a little wrath. And in a little wrath I hid my face from thee for a moment.
precepts.point: But with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee, saith the Lord thy Redeemer.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
“In a little wrath I hid my face from thee for a moment”. That is called slavery. When he hid his face, that is the chains. That is the ships. That is poverty, sickness, death, destruction. That is what all of that sums up right there. Leviticus shows what the little wrath looks like: “And I will set my face against you, and ye shall be slain before your enemies: they that hate you shall reign over you; and ye shall flee when none pursueth you.”

That is a little wrath: slain before our enemies, ruled by them that hate us. And while he hid his face, Psalm 50 shows he kept silence over the wicked who took his covenant in their mouth: “These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself”. God is not intervening in some things. He stays silent, because this is the time for us to get our lives together and repent, to put the pieces of the puzzle in the Bible together. So the so-called white man thought God was like him. “but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes”, and that is what is happening now.

But the little wrath is only for a moment. Isaiah 54:8 ends: “but with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee, saith the Lord thy Redeemer.”

precepts.text: The New Testament says the same thing: blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, and hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David; that we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us; to perform the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant; the oath which he sware to our father Abraham.
precepts.point: And yet for all that, when they be in the land of their enemies, I will not cast them away, neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly, and to break my covenant with them: for I am the Lord their God. But I will for their sakes remember the covenant of their ancestors, whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the heathen. Who said bloodline is not important? The Bible says he will remember the covenant of your ancestors.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
Leviticus 26 says that even “when they be in the land of their enemies”, like today here in America, “I will not cast them away, neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly”. Then: “But I will for their sakes remember the covenant of their ancestors”. Who said bloodline ain’t important? The Bible says he will remember the covenant of your ancestors. Luke 1 is saying the same thing in the New Testament.

“Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David”. The horn of salvation is Christ. He is the king, out of the house of David. “As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began: That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us”. That is what Leviticus 26 is saying: in the land of their enemies he will not cast them away.

“To perform the mercy promised to our fathers”, our ancestors, “and to remember his holy covenant; The oath which he sware to our father Abraham”. That is the covenant of the ancestors in Leviticus 26:45, remembered for their sakes and brought to pass through Christ.

And what is it for? “that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear”. The God who brought our fathers out of Egypt in the sight of the heathen has not broken his covenant with us. He will deliver us out of the hand of our enemies so that we serve him without fear.

precepts.text: I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies: mentally and spiritually you are going to be broken down. The sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them: no courage. And ye shall have no power to stand before your enemies. Think about that spiritually in 2026: when black people get mad at other black people, we show no mercy; we came up with terms for it, turning up, crashing out. But do we have that same level of aggression toward the nations that oppress us? Not at all. We will stand aggressive with each other all day long, but we will not stand before the other nations. And to be clear, we do not advocate violence on anybody; the point is the spirit is not the same.
precepts.point: And I will break the pride of your power: I am going to break your spirit, and I will use the other nations to do it. Now you are bashful; now you have low self-esteem; now you have no confidence.

note.label: The Bold and the Bashful

precepts.why:
This is where the breaking of “the pride of your power” leads. “And upon them that are left alive of you I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies”. Into their minds: mentally and spiritually, you are going to be broken down. Then “the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them”: no courage. And “they shall flee, as fleeing from a sword; and they shall fall when none pursueth.”

“And they shall fall one upon another, as it were before a sword, when none pursueth: and ye shall have no power to stand before your enemies.” Think about that spiritually. Take 2026. When black people get mad at other black people, do we show each other mercy, or do we go full-fledged? We even came up with terms for it: turning up, going savage, crashing out. But do we have that same level of aggression toward white police, or the other nations, or the Chinese? Not at all. We will stand and be aggressive with each other all day long, cuss each other out, beat each other up, kill each other. But we will not stand before the other nations. And to be clear, we do not advocate violence on anybody. The point is that the spirit is not the same toward the nations as it is toward each other.

That faintness is on the face of the African brother who said the colonizers left too early, that we are not prepared to rule ourselves. Not only defeated but subdued: low self-esteem, lack of confidence, self-hate, no faith in his own people. It is seen in a whole country left to itself that looks to the white man, to foreign aid and loans, to save it: a mall built under Chinese direction with not a brick out of place, while what our people build for ourselves has uneven steps and lopsided houses. You can’t do nothing right for yourself. That is what comes of low self-esteem.

So this is the fruit of verse 17, “they that hate you shall reign over you; and ye shall flee when none pursueth you”, and of verse 19, the pride of our power broken. These are the minds the Lord is going to use our brothers to change.

precepts.point: All manner of service: we were their servants, cooking their food, watching their kids, entertaining them, singing for them. Sing us one of the songs of Zion. note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

precepts.why:
Exodus 1:12 says “the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew. And they were grieved because of the children of Israel.” No matter how much they afflicted us, we kept multiplying and growing. And what does it mean that the Egyptians were grieved because of us? They were mad; they were angry.

Leviticus 26:17 explains it: “And I will set my face against you, and ye shall be slain before your enemies: they that hate you shall reign over you; and ye shall flee when none pursueth you.” To be grieved because of the children of Israel means they hated us, and they that hated us reigned over us.

The same way the ancient Egyptians hated us, the so-called white man hated us when we were brought here as slaves. So “the Egyptians made the children of Israel to serve with rigour”: they did not play with us. In ancient Egypt they beat the hell out of us with whips, and in America the same: runaways caught and whooped, lynchings, and still lynching us. Not only America but all the lands we were scattered into are Egypt, but this is the main one, Mystery Babylon.

That is where Mecca is. Your fellow Arab Muslims are selling our people on open slave markets, and you are trying to convince us to become Muslims.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
God’s law says it plainly: “Ye shall make you no idols nor graven image, neither rear you up a standing image, neither shall ye set up any image of stone in your land, to bow down unto it: for I am the Lord your God.” Make no idols, no graven images, and no image of stone to bow down to.

This is what our people do. We go all the way to Mecca to kiss a rock, the Kaaba stone. And they say, we don’t worship the Kaaba stone. Yes, you do. Their own ruling says it: kissing the black stone is an act of worship, done by a Muslim who has no connection to that stone except worshiping Allah by venerating it and following the messenger by doing it. That is bowing down to an image of stone, the very thing the law forbids.

Mecca itself was run down and raggedy in the first known photograph of the Kaaba in 1861. Then they started working with America on oil and got paid, and now people from all over the world call it beautiful. It is still a stone set up to bow down unto.

So Leviticus 26:1 shows why Jeremiah 3 calls it harlotry and polluting the land, and why Israel has a “whore’s forehead” and refuses “to be ashamed”. The Most High is the Lord our God, and he is not in a black stone in Arabia.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
“I have wounded thee with the wound of an enemy, with the chastisement of a cruel one, for the multitude of thine iniquity; because thy sins were increased.” Our sins are increased: the Houston rodeo, black men and women whoring themselves out, filthy and wicked, so bad a dress code had to be put in place; and in Delta State in Nigeria, a festival where women are openly raped in the streets. That is evil. Then: “because thy sins were increased, I have done these things unto thee”.

Moses said it would be so: “And that I also have walked contrary unto them, and have brought them into the land of their enemies”. God walked contrary to us because we kept breaking his laws, and he brought us into the land of our enemies. Then what we must do: “if then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity”.

As we repent, we have to accept that God is right and we are wrong. We have always been wrong. God was just when he punished us. When your child plays in the street or with the light socket, you beat that behind, not because you hate him but so he learns he'll die playing in traffic or with electricity. Some talking doesn't do any good for some kids; you have to rile up on them so they know it's serious. That is what God did with us.

The three holy children did exactly this. In the midst of the fiery furnace, cast in because they would not worship Babylon's god, Azarias prayed: “Blessed art thou, O Lord God of our fathers”, “For thou art righteous in all the things that thou hast done to us: yea, true are all thy works, thy ways are right, and all thy judgments truth.” Then: “for according to truth and judgment didst thou bring all these things upon us because of our sins. For we have sinned and committed iniquity, departing from thee”. Everything God has done to our people is justified, because we revolted against him. They said it because of what Moses said in Leviticus, and what happened to them is a reflection of what will happen to us.

Christianity has taught our people the opposite: to mock a God who got angry at his own people for worshipping a golden calf. But accepting the punishment is the way back, because the next verse is: “Then will I remember my covenant with Jacob”.

precepts.text: Walk in his statutes and keep his commandments, and the rain comes in due season, the land yields her increase, the trees yield their fruit, ye shall eat your bread to the full, and none shall make you afraid.
precepts.point: From the questions: a land flowing with milk and honey is not a magical land of milk. It means a plenteous, fertile land of great landscape, valleys, grass, and fields, with cattle and goats grazing for the milk, and flowers and plants in abundance for the bees to make the honey; a land blessed as the days of heaven upon the earth.

note.label: Exodus 33: My Presence Shall Go with Thee

precepts.why:
“If ye walk in my statutes, and keep my commandments, and do them; Then I will give you rain in due season, and the land shall yield her increase, and the trees of the field shall yield their fruit.” That is what flowing with milk and honey means: a plenteous, fertile land of valleys, grass and fields, with cattle and goats grazing for the milk and flowers and plants for the bees.

“And your threshing shall reach unto the vintage, and the vintage shall reach unto the sowing time: and ye shall eat your bread to the full, and dwell in your land safely. And I will give peace in the land, and ye shall lie down, and none shall make you afraid”. The Lord would drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite, and none would make Israel afraid in it, so long as they walked in his statutes.

precepts.text: Nadab and Abihu offered strange fire which the Lord commanded them not, and fire from the Lord devoured them; I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me.
precepts.point: Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, offered strange fire before the Lord which He commanded them not, and fire went out from the Lord and devoured them; that is what reverencing the sanctuary means.

note.label: Leviticus 26: The Blessings and the Curses

precepts.why:
This is what reverencing the sanctuary means. Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, “offered strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not. And there went out fire from the Lord, and devoured them, and they died before the Lord.”

When you came into the sanctuary you had better come with respect, because the Most High was putting men to death over it. Moses gave the reason: “This is it that the Lord spake, saying, I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me, and before all the people I will be glorified.” And Aaron, their father, held his peace.

So keeping the sabbaths of the Most High and reverencing His sanctuary go together, and the fire that came out on Aaron’s own sons shows how seriously He takes the second one.

precepts.text: If thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord, all these blessings shall come on thee and overtake thee; the same covenant of blessing and curse.
precepts.point: If Israel kept the commandments there would be no famine: rain in due season, the crops continually growing, the harvest coming in on time, and rain in the land even in a drought.

note.label: Leviticus 26: The Blessings and the Curses

precepts.why:
The blessings for walking in the statutes and keeping the commandments are the same blessings and curses read in Deuteronomy the 28th chapter. It is one covenant of blessing and curse.

Moses said, “if thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe and to do all his commandments”, then “the Lord thy God will set thee on high above all nations of the earth: And all these blessings shall come on thee, and overtake thee, if thou shalt hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God.”

Rain in due season and the land yielding her increase is the first of those blessings. If Israel kept the commandments there would be no famine: the crops continually growing, the harvest coming in on time, and rain in the land even in a drought.

precepts.text: Jacob shall return, and shall be in rest, and be quiet, and none shall make him afraid; the future deliverance carries the same promise as this blessing.
precepts.point: That is also how you know the people in the land of Israel today are not the real Jews: this prophecy of rest is not fulfilled on them. When the Most High saves Israel from captivity it will be the same again, and none shall make him afraid.

note.label: Leviticus 26: The Blessings and the Curses

precepts.why:
The Most High would give peace in the land: no enemies able to come against Israel, no war in the land, no one making the people afraid. That was fulfilled in the days of king Solomon, when there was rest on every side.

Jeremiah carries the same promise forward to the future deliverance: “Therefore fear thou not, O my servant Jacob, saith the Lord; neither be dismayed, O Israel: for, lo, I will save thee from afar, and thy seed from the land of their captivity; and Jacob shall return, and shall be in rest, and be quiet, and none shall make him afraid.” The words are the words of the blessing in Leviticus.

That is also how you know the people in the land of Israel today are not the real Jews: this prophecy of rest is not fulfilled on them. When the Most High saves Israel from captivity it will be the same again, and none shall make him afraid.

And power was given unto them over the fourth part of the earth, to kill with sword, and with hunger, and with death, and with the beasts of the earth.”

Sword, hunger, death, and the beasts of the earth are the same instruments of judgment the Most High named in Leviticus.

note.label: Leviticus 26: The Blessings and the Curses

precepts.why:
The Most High said He would walk contrary in fury and would be the one doing it: He would use the enemies, but it would be Him behind it. That is heavy. And eating the flesh of sons and daughters happened in the days of the kings, when the city was besieged and there was such famine that a woman’s son was boiled and eaten.

In the days of the kings “there was a great famine in Samaria: and, behold, they besieged it, until an ass’s head was sold for fourscore pieces of silver, and the fourth part of a cab of dove’s dung for five pieces of silver.” As the king of Israel was passing by upon the wall a woman cried to him for help, and when he asked what ailed her, she answered: “This woman said unto me, Give thy son, that we may eat him to day, and we will eat my son to morrow. So we boiled my son, and did eat him: and I said unto her on the next day, Give thy son, that we may eat him: and she hath hid her son.”

The king could only say, “If the Lord do not help thee, whence shall I help thee?” That is the curse of Leviticus 26 carried out on Israel to the letter.

precepts.why:
Deuteronomy gives the same curse and names the way it comes: by siege. The enemy “shall besiege thee in all thy gates, until thy high and fenced walls come down, wherein thou trustedst, throughout all thy land”.

“And thou shalt eat the fruit of thine own body, the flesh of thy sons and of thy daughters, which the Lord thy God hath given thee, in the siege, and in the straitness, wherewith thine enemies shall distress thee”. The enemies distress them, but it is the Most High walking contrary in fury, using the enemies to do it.

That is how it played out in the siege of Samaria, when the woman boiled her son, and again in 70 AD at Jerusalem.

precepts.text: When ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh; the siege of 70 AD fulfilled this curse.
precepts.point: Eating the flesh of sons and daughters goes into 70 AD, and it also happened in the days of the kings when the city was besieged and there was such famine that a woman's son was boiled and eaten.

note.label: Leviticus 26: The Blessings and the Curses

precepts.why:
Eating the flesh of sons and daughters goes into 70 AD. Christ told them when it would come: “when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.”

Jerusalem compassed with armies is the siege Deuteronomy 28 speaks of, the enemy besieging thee in all thy gates. The siege of 70 AD fulfilled this curse: the same famine that made a woman boil her son in Samaria in the days of the kings came upon Jerusalem when the Romans compassed it.

precepts.text: Remember the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem, who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof; Esau cheered the destruction on.
precepts.point: Scattered among the heathen with a sword drawn out after them: not only the scattering, but death and anguish sent among the people in the lands of the captivity.

note.label: Leviticus 26: The Blessings and the Curses

precepts.why:
The Most High made the cities waste and brought the sanctuaries to desolation, and would not smell the savour of the sweet odours: He was not accepting the sacrifices, and He used the enemy to destroy the sanctuary. The Babylonians destroyed the temple, then the Greeks, then the Romans.

When Babylon came against Jerusalem, Esau stood on the side cheering it on. David records it: “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.” The children of Edom are Esau, and in the day of Jerusalem they urged the destruction on to the foundation.

Then the scattering among the heathen with a sword drawn out after them: not only the scattering, but death and anguish sent among the people in the lands of the captivity.

precepts.text: Among these nations shalt thou find no ease, but a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind, fearing day and night with no assurance of life.
precepts.point: And ye shall perish among the heathen: many of us die in this land and in all the lands where we are scattered, and the land of the enemies eats the people up in oppression.

note.label: Leviticus 26: The Blessings and the Curses

precepts.why:
The faintness sent into the hearts of them that are left alive, in the lands of their enemies, is the same curse Deuteronomy 28 describes for the land of the enemies: “among these nations shalt thou find no ease, neither shall the sole of thy foot have rest: but the Lord shall give thee there a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind”.

And “thy life shall hang in doubt before thee; and thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life: In the morning thou shalt say, Would God it were even! and at even thou shalt say, Would God it were morning!” That is the heart the sound of a shaken leaf chases.

Falling one upon another as it were before a sword when none pursueth is still seen to this day: even at these protests, when the rubber bullets, the tear gas, the water hoses, and the dogs come out, the people stumble and fall over one another trying to get away. And ye shall perish among the heathen: many of us die in this land and in all the lands where we are scattered, and the land of the enemies eats the people up in oppression.

precepts.text: If they bethink themselves in the land of their captivity, and repent, and return unto thee with all their heart, the Most High hears; repentance in captivity brings the covenant back to remembrance.
precepts.point: The land enjoys her sabbaths while she lieth desolate without them, and the people must accept that they were evil and wicked against the Most High, because they despised His judgments and their soul abhorred His statutes.

note.label: Leviticus 26: The Blessings and the Curses

precepts.why:
When the people repent and turn back, the Most High remembers His covenant with Jacob, with Isaac, and with Abraham, the covenant passed down to their children, the children of Israel, and He remembers the land. Solomon prayed for exactly that at the dedication of the house.

“If they sin against thee, (for there is no man that sinneth not,) and thou be angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captives unto the land of the enemy, far or near; Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness”.

That confession is what accepting the punishment of their iniquity looks like: the people owning that they were evil and wicked against the Most High, because they despised His judgments and their soul abhorred His statutes. “And so return unto thee with all their heart, and with all their soul, in the land of their enemies, which led them away captive, and pray unto thee toward their land”: repentance in captivity brings the covenant back to remembrance, and the Most High hears.

precepts.text: If then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they accept the punishment of their iniquity; the Lord speaks here of the heart, not the flesh.
precepts.point: No surgery can circumcise the brain: circumcision of the heart is repentance. You wash you and make you clean by ceasing to do evil, and a young man cleanses his way by taking heed thereto according to the word of the Most High.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

precepts.why:
The physical circumcision is symbolic of spiritual circumcision. The Lord speaks here of the heart, not the flesh: “if then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity”. He has walked contrary unto them and brought them into the land of their enemies, and what has to be humbled is the uncircumcised heart.

The uncircumcised heart is the mind that will not keep the commandments. That is what the second circumcision in Joshua points to: not only the flesh, but the heart.

precepts.text: If ye walk contrary unto me, I will walk contrary unto you also in fury, and chastise you seven times for your sins.
precepts.point: Hearts melting as water is the curse for disobedience: the Most High sends a faintness into the heart, so that the mighty flee as fleeing from a sword and fall when none pursueth, like the athlete in the scary movie suddenly stumbling from sheer fear.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
About three thousand men went up to Ai, “and they fled before the men of Ai.” The way Israel had been winning, they thought they could not lose; but what happened in verse 1 was about to play its part. “And if ye will not for all this hearken unto me, but walk contrary unto me; Then I will walk contrary unto you also in fury; and I, even I, will chastise you seven times for your sins.”

The Lord is the one who wins the battles and gets the victory, not us. Pick out the weakest nation on earth: no matter how strong Israel is physically, if we are not spiritually right with the Lord, he will make us lose, for this fight is not carnal. At Ai the Lord walked contrary to Israel.

precepts.text: I will send a faintness into their hearts; the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them, and they shall flee as fleeing from a sword, and fall when none pursueth.
precepts.point: Hearts melting as water is the curse for disobedience: the Most High sends a faintness into the heart, so that the mighty flee as fleeing from a sword and fall when none pursueth, like the athlete in the scary movie suddenly stumbling from sheer fear.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
“wherefore the hearts of the people melted, and became as water.” Hearts melting as water is the curse for disobedience: “And upon them that are left alive of you I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies; and the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them; and they shall flee, as fleeing from a sword; and they shall fall when none pursueth.”

The Most High sends a faintness into the heart, so that the mighty flee as fleeing from a sword and fall when none pursueth, like the athlete in the scary movie suddenly stumbling from sheer fear. Thirty and six men smitten and Israel chased from before the gate by a people that were but few: that is the faintness sent.

precepts.text: I will give peace in the land, and ye shall lie down, and none shall make you afraid.
precepts.point: Because David meditated in the law, he knew the Lord was his power source. The Lord had promised that five would chase a hundred and a hundred put ten thousand to flight, that He would cause Israel's enemies to be smitten and to flee seven ways. David leaned wholly on that promise.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

precepts.why:
“And I will give peace in the land, and ye shall lie down, and none shall make you afraid: and I will rid evil beasts out of the land, neither shall the sword go through your land.”

The Philistines came up yet again and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim. The Most High hardened the hearts of the nations, so it was of God that they came back. But David was not afraid, because he meditated in the law and knew the promise: peace in the land, and none to make Israel afraid. The Lord was his power source.

precepts.text: Five of you shall chase an hundred, and an hundred of you shall put ten thousand to flight.
precepts.point: Because David meditated in the law, he knew the Lord was his power source. The Lord had promised that five would chase a hundred and a hundred put ten thousand to flight, that He would cause Israel's enemies to be smitten and to flee seven ways. David leaned wholly on that promise.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

precepts.why:
“And five of you shall chase an hundred, and an hundred of you shall put ten thousand to flight: and your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.”

David leaned wholly on that promise. When he enquired this time, the Lord gave him war strategy: “Thou shalt not go up; but fetch a compass behind them, and come upon them over against the mulberry trees.” David sought counsel again rather than assume the last answer.

When he heard “the sound of a going in the tops of the mulberry trees”, then “shall the Lord go out before thee, to smite the host of the Philistines.” The Lord fought before him, and David smote the Philistines from Geba until he came to Gazer. That is how a few chase an hundred and an hundred put ten thousand to flight.

precepts.text: Make no idols nor graven image to bow down to, so the lions in Solomon's house were not for worship.
precepts.point: All Solomon's drinking vessels were gold, and the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were pure gold; silver was nothing accounted of in his days. Once in three years the navy of Tarshish brought gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

precepts.why:
“Ye shall make you no idols nor graven image, neither rear you up a standing image, neither shall ye set up any image of stone in your land, to bow down unto it: for I am the Lord your God.” The law forbids images set up to worship.

Solomon's throne had six steps, “and two lions stood beside the stays.” “And twelve lions stood there on the one side and on the other upon the six steps: there was not the like made in any kingdom.” These standing lions were not graven images to bow down to. They were not worshipped, so the lions in Solomon's house were not for worship.

precepts.text: If they confess their iniquity and their uncircumcised hearts are humbled and they accept the punishment, then the Most High remembers his covenant; humbling brings deliverance.
precepts.point: The people today must likewise humble themselves, relearn to obey the commandments, and accept their condition as righteous judgment from the hand of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 12: Rehoboam Forsakes the Law and Is Humbled

precepts.why:
“If they shall confess their iniquity, and the iniquity of their fathers … if then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity: Then will I remember my covenant with Jacob, and also my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham will I remember; and I will remember the land.”

Humbling brings deliverance. That is what happened under Rehoboam: “They have humbled themselves; therefore I will not destroy them, but I will grant them some deliverance; and my wrath shall not be poured out upon Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.”

“Nevertheless they shall be his servants; that they may know my service, and the service of the kingdoms of the countries.” They had to learn the difference between serving the Most High and serving the kingdoms of the countries.

The people today must likewise humble themselves, relearn to obey the commandments, and accept their condition as righteous judgment from the hand of the Most High: accept the punishment of our iniquity, and he remembers his covenant.

precepts.text: If we keep his statutes and commandments he will give peace in the land, rid evil beasts, and the sword shall not go through our land; keeping the law is how the sword turns.
precepts.point: Arise, O Lord, disappoint him, cast him down, deliver my soul from the wicked which is thy sword. The wicked here is the same deadly enemy and oppressor named in verse 9.

note.label: Psalm 17: Keep Me as the Apple of the Eye

precepts.why:
David cries, “deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword”. The wicked is the same deadly enemy and oppressor named in verse 9, and he is the Most High's sword. Leviticus shows how that sword turns.

“If ye walk in my statutes, and keep my commandments, and do them; Then I will give you rain in due season, and the land shall yield her increase”. Keep his statutes and commandments and we eat our bread to the full and dwell in our land safely. “And I will give peace in the land, and ye shall lie down, and none shall make you afraid: and I will rid evil beasts out of the land, neither shall the sword go through your land.”

Then the sword changes hands: “And ye shall chase your enemies, and they shall fall before you by the sword.” Keeping the law is how the sword turns from being upon us to falling on our enemies. That is the deliverance David asks for from men of the world which have their portion in this life, and it runs with what Bishop taught in the Sabbath class going through Job 20.

precepts.text: If we disobey, they that hate us shall reign over us and we shall be slain before our enemies; this is why the wicked oppressor rules right now, and why our people run when the police come even when innocent.
precepts.point: We are still looking for that deliverance from our strong enemy and them that hate us.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
David was delivered “from my strong enemy, and from them which hated me: for they were too strong for me.” Leviticus tells why they that hate us are too strong for us: “And I will set my face against you, and ye shall be slain before your enemies: they that hate you shall reign over you; and ye shall flee when none pursueth you.”

If we disobey, they that hate us reign over us and we are slain before our enemies. That is why the wicked oppressor rules right now. And “ye shall flee when none pursueth you” is why our people run when the police come, even when they are innocent.

We are still looking for that deliverance from our strong enemy and from them that hate us, the deliverance David sings of when the Lord drew him out of many waters.

precepts.text: Ye shall chase your enemies and five shall chase a hundred and a hundred put ten thousand to flight; this is the power we are looking to receive.
precepts.point: As for God, his way is perfect and the word of the Lord is tried; he is a buckler to all that trust in him.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“For by thee I have run through a troop; and by my God have I leaped over a wall.” That is the strength the Most High girds his people with, and Leviticus tells what it looks like: “And ye shall chase your enemies, and they shall fall before you by the sword. And five of you shall chase an hundred, and an hundred of you shall put ten thousand to flight: and your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.”

Five chase a hundred, and a hundred put ten thousand to flight. This is the power we are looking to receive. It is God that girds us with strength and makes our way perfect, and he is a buckler to all those that trust in him.

precepts.text: Ye shall chase your enemies and they shall fall before you by the sword; five of you shall chase a hundred, and a hundred of you shall put ten thousand to flight.
precepts.point: This is going into the blessing again. Today people say they are blessed as an individual, but we understood that the blessings of God are in Deuteronomy 28, and they refer to our condition as a nation of people. Our enemies fleeing from us is part of that blessing.

note.label: Psalm 68: Let God Arise

precepts.why:
“And ye shall chase your enemies, and they shall fall before you by the sword. And five of you shall chase an hundred, and an hundred of you shall put ten thousand to flight: and your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.” Five chase a hundred, and a hundred put ten thousand to flight. That is the enemies scattered and those that hate him fleeing before him, as David cries for in Psalm 68.

It is a national blessing, like Deuteronomy 28, not an individual one. When we keep the commandments as a nation, the Most High arises and our enemies fall before us by the sword.

precepts.text: They that hate you shall reign over you; the law and the prophets agree.
precepts.point: Nevertheless He regarded their affliction, remembered His covenant, and repented according to His mercies; David prays: save us and gather us from among the heathen. Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

precepts.why:
“And he gave them into the hand of the heathen; and they that hated them ruled over them.” That is the law fulfilled to the letter: “I will set my face against you, and ye shall be slain before your enemies: they that hate you shall reign over you; and ye shall flee when none pursueth you.”

The law and the prophets agree. What Moses wrote in Leviticus, the psalmist records as history, and we live it today with the heathen ruling over us in our own communities, the legal system and the government.

precepts.text: When we are in the land of our enemies the Most High will not cast us away nor destroy us utterly, but will remember the covenant of our ancestors.
precepts.point: This is so important because we are not a cursed people; we are a people under the curses. Because the Lord has been mindful of us, let us see how He has been mindful.

note.label: Psalm 115: Not Unto Us, But Unto Thy Name Give Glory

precepts.why:
“The Lord hath been mindful of us: he will bless us; he will bless the house of Israel”. This is so important, because we are not a cursed people; we are a people under the curses. Here is how he has been mindful of us.
